topDescObelisco: The Obelisk is Buenos Aires' main symbol, located at the intersection of 9 de Julio and Corrientes avenues. The Teatro Colón is one of the world's most important opera houses, with exceptional acoustics and majestic architecture. This package includes a guided tour of both monuments, with theater admission and a walk through the surrounding city area.
topFactsObelisco: Location: Buenos Aires, Argentina|Height: 67 meters|Year: 1936|Visitors: 2 million/year
topDescCanalPanama: The Panama Canal is an engineering marvel connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, inaugurated in 1914. Its locks lift ships over the isthmus mountains on an 82-kilometer journey. The Miraflores Visitor Center allows you to see ships passing up close and learn about the history of this wonder that transformed world trade.
topFactsCanalPanama: Location: Panama City|Inaugurated: 1914|Length: 82 km|Locks: Miraflores and Gatún
topDescCristoRedentor: Christ the Redeemer is a statue of Jesus Christ located atop Corcovado Mountain in Rio de Janeiro. Standing 38 meters tall with 28-meter outstretched arms, it is one of the Seven Wonders of the Modern World. Inaugurated in 1931, it is now Rio de Janeiro's symbol, offering stunning panoramic views of Guanabara Bay.
topFactsCristoRedentor: 38 meters tall|Inaugurated in 1931|Wonder of the World|360° view
topDescTorresDelPaine: Torres del Paine National Park in Chilean Patagonia is one of the world's most iconic trekking destinations. Its three granite towers rise over 2,500 meters above sea level, offering landscapes of glaciers, turquoise lakes, and unique wildlife. The famous W Circuit attracts thousands of hikers from around the world every year.
topDescCartagena: Cartagena de Indias is a colonial gem on Colombia's Caribbean coast. Its walls, cobblestone streets, plazas, and colorful houses transport you to the past. The city offers a blend of history, culture, cuisine, and nearby beaches. The tour includes a visit to San Felipe Castle, the historic center, and a chiva ride.
topDescIguazu: The Iguazu Falls, on the border between Argentina and Brazil, are the world's largest waterfall system with 275 drops plunging from the subtropical jungle. The Devil's Throat, its most imposing cascade, shakes with its roar. Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site, they receive over 1.5 million visitors annually.
topFactsIguazu: Location: Argentina and Brazil|Drops: 275|Devil's Throat: 80 m|Visitors: 1.5 million/year
topDescMachuPicchu: Machu Picchu is one of the world's wonders and the Inca Empire's most impressive legacy. Located atop a mountain in Peru, this historic sanctuary offers breathtaking views and architecture in perfect harmony with its surroundings. The trip includes the train from Cusco, citadel admission, and a specialized guide.
topDescTikal: Tikal was one of the most powerful cities of the Mayan civilization, hidden in the Petén jungle of Guatemala. Its temples, like the Temple of the Great Jaguar, rise above the jungle canopy and were featured in a Star Wars movie. It receives about 1.2 million visitors annually and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
topFactsTikal: Location: Petén, Guatemala|UNESCO Heritage: 1979|Temple IV: 70 m|Visitors: 1.2 million/year
topDescChichenItza: Chichén Itzá was one of the most important cities of the Mayan civilization, located on the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. The Kukulcán Pyramid, also called El Castillo, is its most iconic structure: each equinox, the sun creates a serpent effect descending the stairs. Declared a Wonder of the Modern World and UNESCO World Heritage Site.
topFactsChichenItza: Wonder of the World|UNESCO Heritage|Equinox effect|Mayan civilization
topDescGalapagos: The Galápagos Islands, in Ecuador's Pacific Ocean, inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution. Their giant tortuces, marine iguanas, and blue-footed boobies exist nowhere else on Earth. This volcanic archipelago is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Marine Reserve, receiving over 270,000 visitors annually.
topFactsGalapagos: Location: Pacific Ocean, Ecuador|UNESCO Heritage: 1978|Islands: 19|Unique species: 9,000
